changes: OpenClaw shipped v2026.5.19 on 2026-05-20 20:20 UTC and then followed immediately with v2026.5.20-beta.1 on 2026-05-21 00:11 UTC, keeping the category anchor on a very tight release loop.
ZeroClaw posted v0.8.0-beta-1 on 2026-05-21 01:36 UTC, giving the lightweight Rust lane a fresh product signal.
PicoClaw rolled another nightly on 2026-05-21 01:25 UTC, preserving the strongest daily cadence in the cheap-hardware and edge lane.
Hermes Agent, nanobot, and NanoClaw all showed continued repo activity in the latest snapshot, but without a taxonomy-changing release or positioning shift.
Hermes Agent remains the canonical adjacent benchmark, and the tracked set plus lane map still hold without taxonomy changes.
whyItMatters: The biggest signal is still anchor velocity: OpenClaw is moving from stable release to next-cycle prerelease with almost no idle time, which keeps pressure on the whole field.
ZeroClaw's new beta matters because the lightweight Rust line is still one of the strongest direct competitive answers to OpenClaw's heavier runtime story.
PicoClaw keeps the low-cost always-on deployment wedge visible and credible through near-daily release motion.

This strengthens the existing strategic read rather than changing it: pressure remains concentrated in lighter runtimes, safer runtimes, multi-agent orchestration, learning loops, and more polished execution surfaces.
